    Read first

    • Source. Walls are traced from Cypress Design drawings 1F-P-01, 2F-P-01, 3F-P-01 rev A and 4F-P-01 rev B (1:100, printed February 2018, stamped "for coordination"). Expect about 100 to 200 mm of tracing error on 1/F and up to 300 mm on 2/F to 4/F, where the three drawings disagree with each other by that much. Nesphere must confirm the drawings still match the December works.
    • Ceiling heights are assumed: 2.7 m in the 1/F lobbies, 2.5 m over the 1/F lift lobby and 2.5 m everywhere on 2/F to 4/F. The drawings give none.
    • 2/F to 4/F. Corridors, lift lobbies, the 2/F gym and the 4/F lounge and terrace are modelled. One guest room of each type is furnished and open: room 8 (2/F and 3/F) stands for rooms 8 to 10, room 2 (2/F to 4/F) stands for rooms 2, 3, 5 and 6. The other rooms are closed doors with grey floors in plan view. Rooms 1, 7 and 11 and the 4/F rooms 8 to 10 are one-off layouts and are not furnished yet.
    • Room screens. The drawings mark a wall-mounted screen opposite the bed in each guest room. The first-pass room placements sit on that mark.
    • Fire doors on the routes between the lifts and the corridors are shown held open so you can walk through. In the building they close.
    • 4/F lounge. The room the drawing labels "corridor" has folding glass doors along the terrace side, shown open. Daylight and weather on that wall need checking before a work or a screen goes there.
    • Upper-floor finishes are placeholders. No render of a corridor or guest room was supplied, so walls are plain white, with carpet and timber stand-ins.
    • Stair to the lift lobby: 7 risers counted on the drawing, modelled at 165 mm each, so the lift lobby sits 1,155 mm above the entrance lobby.
    • Glass doors. The drawing shows two sliding glass panels that park in front of the two walls beside the opening. The deck puts feature works on exactly those walls. Walk up to the doors to see the clash.
    • Reception wall. On the drawing the wall behind the desk is 2.4 m wide between the corner and the column. Nesphere's render shows a much wider wall, with their logo on it and windows beside it. One of the two is out of date.
    • Lounge glazing on the west side is read from the thin double line on the drawing. The north wall is modelled solid.
    • Not modelled: the 1/F admin office, the hatched non-scope areas, the stairs, back-of-house rooms and the insides of the bathrooms.
    • Screens use approximate outer sizes for Samsung The Frame worked out from the diagonal. Check them against the current Hong Kong spec sheet before anything is issued.
    • Finishes follow the renders: forest green and deep red plaster, pale terrazzo. Artwork images are stand-ins until the inventory is chosen.
